newsitem.title: NORWAY: Loadings resume at Statfjord, Gullfaks and Snorre.
newsitem.headline: Loadings resume at Statfjord, Gullfaks and Snorre.

text.p: Oil production at the North Sea Statfjord, Gullfaks and Snorre platforms was returning to normal on Saturday after the resumption of offshore loadings, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said.
"We started loading again during the night," Statoil spokesman Lars Gunnar Dahle said. "This morning there were tankers at all five loading buoys. Another five tankers were waiting for their turn."
"We expect to back at full production today at Statfjord, Gullfaks and Snorre. These things go quickly once loadings resume," he said. "The weather outlook looks alright."
Stormy weather forced Statfjord and Snorre to curb output on Tuesday and Wednesday because of disruptions to loadings and burgeoning storage and were followed early on Thursday by Gullfaks.
On Thursday, with waves rising to about eight metres, output at the fields was down to 425,000 barrels per day, roughly one third of normal levels.
The maximum permitted wave height for shuttle tankers to moor at offshore loading buoys is 4.5 metres.
Statfjord alone pumps about 380,000 barrels per day (bpd) and processes oil from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre development.
